verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā nāgadatto kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Nāgadatta was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nāgadatto atikālena gāmaṁ pavisati, atidivā paṭikkamati.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Nāgadatta had been entering the village too early and returning late in the day.

verses.pali: Atha kho yā tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmato nāgadattassa anukampikā atthakāmā āyasmantaṁ nāgadattaṁ saṁvejetukāmā yenāyasmā nāgadatto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ nāgadattaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the deity haunting that forest had sympathy for Nāgadatta, wanting what’s best for him. So they approached him wanting to stir him up, and recited these verses:
and returning too late in the day,
I’m afraid for Nāgadatta; he’s reckless,
May he not come under the King of Death’s power,
under the sway of the terminator!”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā nāgadatto tāya devatāya saṁvejito saṁvegamāpādīti.
verses.english: Impelled by that deity, Venerable Nāgadatta was struck with a sense of urgency.
